title: Mercury
text: Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System and the closest planet to the Sun. Its year lasts about 88 Earth days.

title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae, and some bacteria use light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen is released as a by-product.

title: Great Barrier Reef
text: The Great Barrier Reef is located in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, Australia. It is the world's largest coral reef system.

title: Marie Curie
text: Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity. She received Nobel Prizes in Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911.

title: Python Language
text: Python is a high-level programming language created by Guido van Rossum. Its first public release was in 1991.

title: Amazon River
text: The Amazon River flows through northern South America and has the largest drainage basin in the world. It empties into the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Hubble Space Telescope
text: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990. It was named after astronomer Edwin Hubble.

title: Mona Lisa
text: The Mona Lisa is a portrait painted by Leonardo da Vinci. It is displayed at the Louvre Museum in Paris, France.

title: Human Heart
text: The human heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles. It pumps blood through the circulatory system.

title: Mount Everest
text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level. It lies on the border between Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region.

title: Japanese Shinkansen
text: Japan's Shinkansen is a network of high-speed railway lines. The first line began service between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka in 1964.

title: DNA
text: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid. It carries genetic instructions used in the growth, development, and functioning of living organisms.

title: The Moon
text: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. Its gravity is a major cause of ocean tides on Earth.

title: French Revolution
text: The French Revolution began in 1789. It transformed France's political and social structure and led to the end of the Bourbon monarchy.

title: Penguins
text: Penguins are flightless seabirds found almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere. They use their wings as flippers while swimming.

title: Periodic Table
text: The periodic table organizes chemical elements by atomic number. Dmitri Mendeleev published an early influential version in 1869.

title: Internet Protocol
text: Internet Protocol, commonly abbreviated IP, provides rules for addressing and routing data packets across networks. IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses.

title: Sahara Desert
text: The Sahara is a desert in North Africa. It is the largest hot desert in the world.

title: Beethoven
text: Ludwig van Beethoven was a German composer and pianist. His Symphony No. 9 includes a choral final movement based on Friedrich Schiller's Ode to Joy.

title: Vaccines
text: Vaccines train the immune system to recognize a specific pathogen or part of a pathogen. They can reduce the risk of infectious disease.

title: Turing Machine
text: A Turing machine is an abstract model of computation introduced by Alan Turing in 1936. It manipulates symbols on an unbounded tape according to rules.

title: World Wide Web
text: The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee while working at CERN. The first website went live in 1991.

title: Coffee
text: Coffee is brewed from roasted coffee beans, which are the seeds of fruits from Coffea plants. Brazil is a major producer of coffee.

title: Solar Eclipse
text: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, blocking all or part of the Sun's light for observers on Earth.

title: Statue of Liberty
text: The Statue of Liberty is a monument in New York Harbor. France gave it to the United States, and it was dedicated in 1886.
